questions.title: Solar panel light intensity — SI quantities, uncertainty & efficiency

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Charge is not an SI base quantity — the SI base quantities are current, length and time (with mass, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity).

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: efficiency = useful output power / total input power = (160 / 750) × 100 = 21%

parts.answer: The new panel has a smaller area, so with the same incident intensity its input (total) power is less than the original panel's. The useful power output is the same, so efficiency = useful output / total input is greater for the new panel.

questions.title: Skydiver terminal velocity and parachute — acceleration & momentum

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: The curve becomes horizontal at the end, so the terminal velocity is 39 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
Draw the tangent to the curve at t = 9.0 s and measure its gradient:
a = Δv/Δt = (44 − 26) / (18 − 0) ≈ 1.0 m s⁻² (0.9–1.1 m s⁻² accepted).

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
Resultant force = mg − F(drag) = 68 × 9.81 − 1800 = 667 − 1800 = −1133 N
a = ΣF/m = 1133 / 68 = 17 m s⁻², directed upwards (the drag force exceeds the weight, so the acceleration opposes the motion).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Between t₂ and t₃ the speed decreases, so the drag force decreases; the resultant (upward) force therefore decreases, and the magnitude of the acceleration decreases to zero as the constant velocity of 5.7 m s⁻¹ is reached.

questions.title: Thermistor circuit — Kirchhoff's laws and potential divider

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Kirchhoff's second law: the sum of the electromotive forces (e.m.f.s) around a closed loop equals the sum of the potential differences around that loop (conservation of energy).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
From Fig. 5.2 at 190 °C, Rᵧ = 25 Ω. Using the potential-divider formula:
Vᵧ = E × Rᵧ/(Rᵧ + Rᵥ) = 9.0 × 25 / (25 + 450) = 225 / 475 = 0.47 V

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: Increasing Rᵥ increases the total resistance of the series circuit, so the current in the circuit decreases. With V = IR and Rᵧ unchanged, the p.d. across Y therefore decreases.

questions.title: Diffraction grating — number of bright fringes

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
d sin θ = nλ, with maximum order when sin θ = 1:
n(max) = d/λ = 3.8 × 10⁻⁶ / (520 × 10⁻⁹) = 7.31, so n = 7 on each side of the central maximum.
Total number of bright fringes = 7 + 1 + 7 = 15

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The frequency of red light is less than the frequency of the original light (c = fλ is constant and red light has a longer wavelength).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Red light has a longer wavelength, so the maximum order n(max) = d/λ is smaller. The number of bright fringes formed is therefore fewer.

parts.answer: A particle composed of one quark and one antiquark belongs to the class of mesons (also accepted: hadrons).

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
Q: strange quark has charge −⅓e; total charge −1e, so the second quark must be an antiquark of charge −⅔e — anti-up (or anti-charm or anti-top).
R: anti-up has charge −⅔e; total charge 0, so the second quark must have charge +⅔e — up (or charm or top).
